items.title: Last-minute push seeks to keep Canadian winter tradition thriving in Mississauga
items.summary: City officials are making a last-minute push to ensure a Canadian winter tradition returns to as many Mississauga neighbourhoods as possible in the coming months. Dozens of volunteers will soon be out in force to help create and maintain natural ice rinks at parks throughout the city so residents can participate in two of Canada’s favourite outdoor pastimes — ice skating or a pickup hockey game on the ice surfaces. The City of Mississauga says volunteer rink-keepers are being sought to help maintain the outdoor recreation spots. Those interested must apply by Nov. 15. With only a few days left to apply, volunteers are specifically being sought to help maintain rinks at:​ “While winter may seem far away, natural ice rinks don’t happen without local volunteers,” the City of Mississauga said Wednesday in a plea for more helpers. “The city provides the equipment and support. ​” Volunteers for the city’s Natural Ice Rinks Program must be 14 years of age or older and comfortable working outdoors in cold temperatures, likely in the late evening any day of the week. Whether it’s a leisurely skate at Celebration Square in Mississauga’s downtown core or a pickup game of shinny hockey at any one of the dozens of natural ice rinks in neighbourhood parks, city officials say the ice surfaces are usually ready for skaters by sometime in late December or into January, when the weather is cold enough. “Natural ice rinks are a longstanding winter tradition in Mississauga and across Canada,” the City of Mississauga said earlier this fall in reintroducing the annual program.

items.title: 5 unique things you can borrow for free in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon
items.summary: When money’s tight, it’s good to know that there’s an easy way to borrow all kinds of items without spending a dime. The Share, Reuse, Repair Hub is a digital resource that connects people with local businesses and events in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon, encouraging them to share, repair, swap, borrow and buy second-hand instead of purchasing new. It also offers opportunities to learn practical skills and explore the circular economy, helping make everyday life more affordable and communities more sustainable. Here are 5 unique things you might not have known you can borrow from libraries and centres across Peel Region for free (availability varies by location): Sports equipment: Get active and play some outdoor sports without needing to invest in any new equipment beforehand. Find 60 sports equipment lockers across Peel Region, full of equipment such as soccer balls, basketballs, footballs and frisbees that can all be borrowed for free. Musical instruments: Learn to play music without the commitment of purchasing a brand new instrument. Guitars, ukuleles, keyboards, and even some less common options like glockenspiels are available to be borrowed. Some instruments include options for both right and left-handed players, cases, straps and electronic tuners. A GoPro and accessories: For the enthusiast photographers and videographers out there, items like the GoPro HERO 7 & 11 are ready to be loaned out. This small, durable action camera can be used to capture high-quality photos and videos during sports, adventures, travel, and other exciting activities. Telescopes: The best way to get a glimpse of the beautifully starry sky is with a telescope. Telescope kits include a telescope, travel bag, accessories and guide, perfect for terrestrial and celestial viewing on the go.

items.title: Exhibit celebrates Mississauga’s musical legends, from Oscar Peterson to Billy Talent
items.summary: Some of Canada’s biggest musical names have connections to Mississauga, and there is still time to explore their history through an exhibition featuring rare instruments, stage outfits and other memorabilia. But the clock is ticking for anyone hoping to catch A City in Tune: Mississauga’s Greatest Hits, an exhibition at the historic Adamson Estate that closes Dec. 27. Presented by the Museums of Mississauga, the exhibition takes visitors on a musical journey spanning nearly 70 years, highlighting the performers, innovators and venues that helped shape the city’s music scene. Among the artists featured are rock legends Triumph, internationally known band Billy Talent, guitarist Donna Grantis, jazz great Oscar Peterson and rockabilly star Ronnie Hawkins. For fans of Triumph, there are some particularly interesting pieces on display, including an autographed guitar belonging to guitarist Rik Emmett and a drum kit associated with drummer Gil Moore. Visitors can also see Donna Grantis’ guitar and stage-worn tour outfits, along with memorabilia, equipment and other tour artifacts connected to Billy Talent. The exhibition also features large-scale portraits of some of Mississauga’s best-known musicians, archival materials, a map highlighting important music venues and attractions, and curated playlists featuring artists connected to the city. The collection offers a look beyond the familiar names, exploring the people and places that helped build Mississauga’s reputation as a music destination.

items.title: Canada Post to Phase Out Door-to-Door Mail Delivery in Mississauga Starting 2027
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Canada Post will begin switching thousands of Mississauga households from door-to-door mail delivery to community mailboxes starting in 2027. The outlet reported the move is part of a nationwide plan to convert about four million addresses still receiving mail at the door, with the Crown corporation aiming to finish within five years. Mississauga's rollout will run in four conversion periods from October 2027 to November 2028, organized by the first three characters of each postal code, the report said. The first neighbourhoods affected will be those with postal codes beginning with L5M and L5N, set to convert in October 2027, according to insauga.com. Residents can use that postal-code schedule to estimate roughly when their own delivery will end, the outlet noted.

items.title: Ontario's Ban on Speed Cameras Marks One Year Since Mississauga's 22 Devices Went Dark
items.summary: According to insauga.com, it has been one year since Mississauga's automated speed-enforcement cameras last captured images of speeding drivers on city roads. The outlet reported the city's 22 roadside cameras took their final photos on Nov. 13, 2025, before Ontario's ban on the devices took effect province-wide the next day. Mississauga and other municipalities opposed the ban, arguing the cameras had helped cut serious and fatal collisions, insauga.com said. Premier Doug Ford had called the cameras a cash grab, the report noted. The ban, enacted under the province's Bill 56, eliminated more than 700 speed-enforcement devices operating in 40 municipalities since 2019. Mississauga's commissioner of transportation and works, Sam Rogers, said losing the cameras would add pressure on the city's road-safety initiatives, according to insauga.com.

items.title: Ward 2 and Ward 7 Get New Faces as Mississauga's 2026-2030 Council Takes Oaths Nov. 16
items.summary: Mississauga's newly elected city council will be sworn in at an inaugural meeting on Nov. 16, according to insauga.com. The outlet reported that mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo, who is moving up from the Ward 2 council seat, will take his oath of office alongside two first-time councillors and nine returning members for the 2026-2030 term. Tom Ellard will take over the Ward 2 seat Tedjo is vacating, while Lucas Alves succeeds Dipika Damerla in Ward 7 after she ran unsuccessfully for mayor, insauga.com said. The meeting is open to the public on a first-come, first-seated basis, according to the report. Two days later, on Nov. 18, the new council will hold its first general committee meeting to begin addressing city business, the outlet noted. The council's term runs until late 2030.
